preface: MAMM 2026 (the 8th International Conference on Microactuators, Microsensors and Micromechanisms) provides an international forum for researchers, students, and industry professionals to present recent research findings, exchange knowledge, and promote interdisciplinary collaboration in microsystems technology. The conference highlights advances in micro-robotics, micro-IC packaging, micro-scale heat transfer, microsurgical technologies, unmanned aerial systems, and miniature rigid-body and compliant mechanisms.

MAMM 2026 is hosted by National Chung Hsing University, Taiwan, and jointly organized with the International Federation for the Promotion of Mechanism and Machine Science (IFToMM) and the Nanotechnology and Micro System Association, Taiwan. Building upon previous editions held in Aachen, Durgapur, Timisoara, Ilmenau, Hyderabad, and Ho Chi Minh City, MAMM 2026 will be held on 5–7 November 2026 at the Sun Moon Lake Teachers’ Hostel, Nantou, Taiwan. We wish to express our sincere gratitude to our distinguished speakers, generous sponsors, and all committee members who have dedicated their time and effort to organizing this event, and we look forward to welcoming you to MAMM 2026.

Only full and excellent papers are selected for publication in the conference proceedings, indexed by Springer (Scopus and Ei Compendex). A special session entitled “Compliant Mechanism” has been established for this edition, chaired by Prof. Ashok Kumar Pandey (Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad, India) and Prof. Lena Zentner (Technische Universität Ilmenau, Germany).

papers.abstract: This paper addresses the problem of insufficient torque in active ankle prostheses for stair locomotion. An experimental analysis of human stair ascent and descent was conducted to identify the required kinematic and dynamic characteristics. A BLDC-driven ankle prosthesis was developed and optimized through control system tuning. The results show that the output torque increased from 0.44 N·m to 6.38 N·m (≈14.5×), enabling stable and repeatable cyclic motion. Although the achieved torque remains below the physiological level (~17 N·m), the prototype successfully reproduces key kinematic features of human movement. These findings demonstrate that torque enhancement is critical for enabling stair locomotion and confirm the feasibility of the proposed approach. Future work will focus on further torque improvement and adaptive control strategies

papers.abstract: Bridge-type compliant mechanisms (BTCMs) are frequently used in precision positioning devices to enlarge the short travel provided by piezoelectric actuators. Their static response depends strongly on flexure-hinge geometry, with the minimum hinge thickness playing a particularly important role. This work develops a compliance-matrix analytical model for a BTCM containing eight identical right-circular flexure hinges. Hinge flexibility is obtained from a variable-cross-section beam representation and then assembled at mechanism level through coordinate transformations, compliance superposition, and reduction of constrained degrees of freedom. The effects of varying hinge thickness from 1 to 5 mm are quantified in terms of displacement amplification, input stiffness, and output stiffness. The analytical model predicts that the amplification ratio falls from 8.43 to 1.68 as the hinge becomes thicker, while both stiffness measures increase substantially. Three-dimensional finite-element simulations confirm the same decreasing amplification trend, although noticeable quantitative differences appear for intermediate thickness values. The resulting model is therefore suitable as a compact tool for preliminary thickness selection and for studying the trade-off between motion amplification and stiffness in bridge-type compliant mechanisms.

papers.abstract: Objectives: Multiomics-based prognostic models have demonstrated substantial success in predicting clinical outcomes across various cancers. However, these models often incorporate large numbers of molecular features, making biological interpretation challenging and obscuring the contribution of specific cancer-related processes. To address this limitation, we developed a cancer stemness-guided multiomics framework that focuses exclusively on molecular features associated with cancer stemness within a given tumor type. By restricting model construction to stemness-related signatures, our approach aims to improve our understanding of the underlying cancer biology while presenting the impact of cancer stemness on patient survival and disease prognosis. Methods: We developed a stemness-guided graph learning framework that integrates tumor stemness information to enable biologically informed representation learning for cancer survival prediction. Specifically, a stemness-guided node-gating mechanism was designed to modulate message aggregation according to gene-level stemness priors, thereby enhancing the extraction of molecular representations associated with cancer progression. The model was trained using The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) discovery cohort and its generalizability was systematically assessed in independent external validation cohorts. Model performance was evaluated using the concordance index (C-index) and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) as the primary measures of prognostic discrimination. Results: The proposed stemness-guided framework demonstrated superior prognostic performance compared with existing approaches, including the Multi-level Graph Neural Network and the interpretable convolutional neural network PathCNN. In addition to improved predictive accuracy, the framework exhibited enhanced stability and risk stratification capability. Using malignant brain cancer as a representative case study, the model achieved an AUROC of 0.77 in the TCGA cohort, outperforming all comparator models. Survival analysis further revealed significant separation between risk groups, with patients classified into the high-risk cohort exhibiting a 2.25-fold higher risk of death than those in the low-risk cohort. Conclusions: The proposed cancer stemness-guided multiomics framework improved prognostic prediction and risk stratification performance relative to existing graph-based and deep learning approaches. By incorporating stemness-related biological priors into representation learning, the framework provides a more interpretable strategy for investigating the contribution of cancer stemness to patient outcomes. These findings support the prognostic relevance of stemness-associated molecular features and demonstrate the potential of biologically informed machine learning frameworks for cancer prognostication. Further validation in larger independent cohorts and across diverse cancer types is warranted.

papers.abstract: The shock sensor provides protection to equipment during operation by detecting sudden speed changes. This article presents the design of a micro-level shock sensor that is able to detect acceleration with bidirectional on a axis. This structure includes a center mass, and a frame mass are connected through inner beams and outer beams. This design flexibility is exploited here for the design of a bistable mechanism with nearly equal switching acceleration with bidirectional on a axis. The sensor is based on a bi-stable mechanism so that it will be able to operate with high precision and saving a large amount of energy. An investigation of the characteristics of shock sensor is conducted using finite element methods and numerical calculations. Acceleration values of 20 g with bidirectional on a axis are detected by an optimized shock sensor structure.

papers.abstract: Thermoelectric generators (TEGs) offer a promising route for converting waste heat into electrical energy; however, the practical implementation of high-performance micro-TEGs (μTEGs) is limited by the material performance and mechanical fragility of thick bismuth telluride (Bi₂Te₃) films. Although thick thermoelectric layers are required to sustain sufficient temperature gradients, conventional fabrication often induces residual stress, leading to cracking and structural failure. In this work, we introduce a materials design strategy by incorporating bio-derived chitosan nanofibers (ChNFs) into the electrodeposition process. The amino and hydroxyl functional groups of ChNFs promote interfacial bonding and nucleation, enabling the rapid growth of dense, crack-free composite films with thicknesses up to 1000 µm. The introduction of ChNFs also creates abundant phonon-scattering interfaces, significantly reducing lattice thermal conductivity from 1.48 to 0.29 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ and resulting in a 303% increase in the room-temperature figure of merit (ZT), from 0.12 to 0.50. At an optimal loading of 0.012 wt%, the composite films exhibit a 15% increase in hardness while maintaining structural integrity. These results demonstrate a multifunctional materials design strategy that simultaneously enhances thermoelectric performance, mechanical robustness, and fabrication scalability. The ChNF–Bi₂Te₃ nanocomposites provide a viable green pathway for developing reliable thick films for next-generation self-powered electronics and compact waste-heat harvesting systems.

papers.abstract: Refining a finite element mesh raises cost much faster than it raises accuracy, and machine tool studies rarely quantify how much numerical error remains. This investigation swept 37 tetrahedral meshes (4–40 mm) on a tilting-rotary CNC spindle head, tracking thirteen responses, and bounded the error in each using the Grid Convergence Index with Richardson extrapolation. Uncertainty spans three orders of magnitude: 3.18% (deformation), 55.33% (stress), 52.75% (strain), and 200.47% (strain energy). This spread is shown to cap regression accuracy regardless of algorithm or sample count. Among four benchmarked models, Random Forest ranks first (mean R² = 0.9373) and LS Boost reaches R² = 0.9940 on deformation. Deployed as a mesh optimizer, the surrogate collapses a 671.6-minute sweep into sub-second inference and identifies a mesh 96.8% smaller than the converged configuration while all responses remain within the post-convergence plateau. Beyond mesh selection, the framework supports interactive design iteration, automated CAE meshing, and digital-twin deployment, while the GCI budget reveals in advance which responses merit analysis investment.

papers.abstract: Low-frequency electromagnetic waves offer deep penetration for cross-medium communication, biomedical implants, and sensing, but conventional antennas suffer from impractically large sizes. While magnetoelectric (ME) antennas reduce size via mechanical driving, they require high bias magnetic fields and exhibit limited coupling efficiency. This work proposes a structural approach using a microstripe magnetostriction layer to overcome these constraints. Metglas stripes were patterned via lithography and bonded onto a PZT plate to form 20 × 5 mm bimorph ME samples. Equivalent circuit modeling predicts that the high-aspect-ratio stripes minimize demagnetization, enhance the low-bias piezomagnetic coefficient, and reduce mechanical damping. Experimental results confirm strong magnetic anisotropy and show that the microstripe device halves the optimal bias field. Compared to continuous laminates, it demonstrates a ~2× improvement in direct ME coupling (4.2 V/cm·Oe at 8.9 Oe) and a ~4.5× enhancement in radiated magnetic field at 1 m. The antenna achieves a magnetic detection limit of 9 pT, a noise floor of 1.82 pT/√Hz at 72 kHz, and an enhanced field-of-view (52°). These results demonstrate microstripe patterning as a powerful strategy for compact, low-bias ME antennas in bio-implants and underwater communication.

papers.abstract: As the diabetic population continues to rise, the demand for chronic wound care is increasingly urgent. However, the high costs of existing advanced therapies, such as stem cell treatments, limit their clinical penetration. To address this, this study aims to establish three-dimensional (3D) skin models as innovative alternative testing platforms. For model construction, rat tail collagen is first mixed with WS1 fibroblasts to form a collagen base. Subsequently, HaCaT cells are seeded and maintained in submerged culture for three days, before being transferred to an air-liquid interface (ALI) for ten days to induce skin differentiation. Currently, the establishment of the healthy model has been preliminarily completed, and histological sectioning alongside staining analysis is underway. Future work will expand to establish three additional pathological models: a hyperglycemic and inflammatory model, a melanoma model, and a combined pathological model integrating high-glucose, inflammation, and melanoma. Utilizing these four skin models, we will systematically evaluate three candidate drugs: Ectoin, aimed at counteracting hyperglycemic damage and reducing pro-inflammatory cytokines; CIC2, effective in promoting dermal repair and strengthening the skin barrier; and recombinant Serglycin, utilized to promote keratinocyte migration and dermal remodeling. Ultimately, this platform is expected to become a crucial tool for future research in skin diseases, wound healing, and oncology. It possesses significant application value as a pre-clinical testing system for developing new drugs and cosmetics, thereby effectively reducing the reliance on animal experiments.

papers.abstract: The dynamic behavior of compliant mechanisms is mainly governed by their geometry, mass distribution and material parameters. Predicting their natural frequencies with analytical methods is a well-studied and still active area of research. The inverse problem though — determining an unknown modulus of elasticity from a measured natural frequency — has received comparatively little attention, despite its practical relevance for monolithically manufactured, non-destructively testable compliant mechanisms. This paper extends a previously developed analytical, transfer-matrix-method (TMM) based framework for the dynamic analysis of compliant mechanisms to inverse material characterization. By reformulating the governing equations so that the Young’s modulus E is treated as the dependent variable, the modulus of an unknown or uncharacterized material can be extracted from a single natural frequency measurement together with the geometrically determined volume and the mass-derived density. The approach is validated experimentally on a monolithic compliant parallel guide mechanism. The natural frequency is obtained from a free-vibration decay test recorded with a dual optical displacement sensor setup. The resulting Young’s modulus deviates by only 2.87\ % from the reference value, confirming the suitability of the method as an efficient, non-destructive diagnostic tool for the material characterization of compliant mechanisms.

papers.title: Development of a 3D Microfluidic Co-Culture Chip Model for Cross-Platform Comparison of Lung Adenocarcinoma Morphology and Spatial Migration
papers.authorsLine: Zi-Yi Chen and Bill Cheng*
papers.abstract: Understanding how lung tumors adapt their morphology and spatial migration across microenvironments is essential in cancer research. Conventional two-dimensional 2D monolayer cultures lack three-dimensional 3D tissue architecture, making it necessary to evaluate whether in vitro models accurately mimic authentic in vivo tumor structures. Meanwhile, although mouse xenografts and patient tissue sections provide native microenvironments, observing live-cell dynamic behavior in real time remains challenging, making it necessary to evaluate if in vitro 3D tumor models can reproduce in vivo phenomena. To bridge these platforms, this study aims to build a controllable 3D microfluidic chip model to compare tumor spatial distributions across cell chips, animal models, and clinical biopsies. A549 lung adenocarcinoma spheroids were embedded into a 3D collagen hydrogel within ibidi chips to establish a co-culture system with THP-1 monocytes. To date, static chip culture with and without THP-1 cells has been completed, along with 3D confocal microscopy imaging. Future work will integrate microfluidic channels for dynamic fluid flow testing and perform comprehensive 3D spatial comparisons among all three models.

papers.title: Development of a Standardized Feline Renal Ultrasonographic Image Database for Investigating Cortical Anisotropic Backscattering Artifact in Chronic Kidney Disease
papers.authorsLine: Yu-Xuan Li*, Bill Cheng* and Kuan-Sheng Chen*
papers.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is one of the most prevalent chronic disorders in cats and is often diagnosed only after substantial loss of renal function because of its nonspecific clinical manifestations during the early stages. Renal ultrasonography is a non-invasive imaging modality routinely used for evaluating renal morphology and structural abnormalities in veterinary practice. Among the ultrasonographic findings, cortical anisotropic backscattering artifact (CABA) has recently attracted attention as a potential imaging feature associated with feline CKD. However, the lack of standardized imaging datasets has limited systematic investigation and quantitative analysis of this phenomenon. In this study, a standardized feline renal ultrasonographic image database was established by integrating renal ultrasound images with corresponding clinical information and biochemical parameters. The database includes standardized image annotations, such as kidney laterality, imaging plane, image quality, and CABA status, providing a consistent framework for image organization and analysis. Furthermore, the relationship between CABA and renal function indicators, including serum creatinine concentration and CKD stage, will be investigated to evaluate the clinical significance of CABA as a potential imaging biomarker. The established database provides a valuable resource for quantitative image analysis and future development of artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostic systems. This work is expected to facilitate standardized renal ultrasound interpretation, improve the evaluation of feline chronic kidney disease, and promote the integration of medical imaging and intelligent diagnostic technologies in veterinary medicine.

papers.title: 建立三維仿生外血視網膜屏障模型，探索缺氧下rhSRGN的潛力
papers.authorsLine: Jing-Mei Wang and Bill Cheng*
papers.abstract: Wet age-related macular degeneration (wAMD) is commonly characterized by outer blood-retinal barrier (oBRB) disruption associated with pathologic choroidal neovascularization under hypoxic stress. Standard anti- vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) injections temporarily inhibit neovascularization, but their rapid ocular clearance necessitates frequent reinjections, which often limits therapeutic efficacy and patient compliance. Therefore, identifying alternative biomacromolecules capable of sustained local retention may help modulate the angiogenic microenvironment. Recombinant human serglycin (rhSRGN) represents a promising candidate, owing to its glycosaminoglycan (GAG) chains. These sulfated GAG chains are known to bind and localize extracellular VEGF, potentially prolonging its intraocular retention and reducing the need for frequent reinjections. Here, we investigate whether rhSRGN can preserve oBRB integrity under pathological stress. To test this hypothesis, we are developing a biomimetic 3D oBRB model using a 12-well hanging insert co-culture system. Human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) and human retinal pigment epithelial cells (ARPE-19) are being co-cultured to reproduce the physiological architecture of the choroid-RPE interface. Optimal individual culture conditions for both cell types have been established, and ongoing work focuses on integrating them. Following system optimization, we plan to introduce a hypoxia-induced model to simulate the wAMD microenvironment and evaluate the potential protective effects of rhSRGN under these conditions. We will monitor cellular responses and barrier function alterations through preliminary morphological observations as well as molecular and biochemical analyses. This in vitro system is intended to provide a preliminary evaluation of rhSRGN's protective effects in this context, offering initial insight relevant to wAMD.

papers.title: A Microfluidic 3D Colorectal Cancer Spheroid Model Incorporating Monocytes for Tumor Microenvironment Recapitulation and Drug Efficacy Evaluation
papers.authorsLine: Yi-Jia Su and Bill Cheng*
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer remains a major global health challenge, and the efficacy of chemotherapy is often limited by poor drug penetration and the complex tumor microenvironment (TME). Conventional two-dimensional (2D) cell cultures fail to accurately reproduce these physiological barriers and the TME, resulting in limited predictive value for preclinical drug evaluation. To address these limitations, this study aims to establish a three-dimensional (3D) colorectal cancer spheroid model integrated with a microfluidic system that provides dynamic perfusion conditions while incorporating monocytes as an immune component to better recapitulate the TME. This platform will also be used to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of Metformin, a repurposed drug with growing interest in oncology, Gemcitabine, whose therapeutic effects in 3D colorectal cancer spheroid models remain largely unexplored, and a laboratory-developed monocyte-mediated drug carrier (MMDC), which utilizes monocytes to de-liver drug to the target site for the treatment of colorectal cancer. As the first stage of this work, HCT116 spheroid formation and morphology are being evaluated using initial seeding densities of 500 and 1,000 cells per well. As monocytes play important roles in tumor progression and immune regulation within the TME, THP-1 monocytes have been incorporated into the model to investigate their interactions with HCT116 spheroids. Future work will integrate this immune-relevant co-culture model into the microfluidic platform and evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of Metformin, Gemcitabine, and MMDC against colorectal cancer.

papers.abstract: This study proposes a method combining a custom-built microfluidic chip with electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) for the semi-quantitative analysis of dielectric particles. Thirty microfluidic chips were fabricated for the experiments. Deionized water (DI water), a single microplastic particle (1 MP), and two microplastic particles (2 MPs) were respectively injected into the electrode sensing regions of the chips. Subsequently, sampling and measurements were conducted using an LCR meter within a frequency range of 20 kHz to 300 kHz. Experimental results demonstrate that the addition of microplastics alters the electrical characteristics of the fluid. Observations from the measurement data indicate a stable trend in impedance magnitudes within the 20 kHz to 100 kHz frequency range, following the order of "DI water > 1 MP > 2 MPs". Simultaneously, DI water exhibits stronger capacitive properties, whereas the presence of microplastics causes a phase angle shift in the low-frequency band. These findings confirm that by comprehensively analyzing the variations in impedance magnitude and phase angle within specific frequency bands, the proposed system can effectively identify the presence and relative quantity of dielectric particles, further verifying the feasibility of dielectric particle detection via EIS integrated with microfluidic chips.

papers.title: AI-Based Virtual Driving Assessment for Joint Replacement Patients
papers.authorsLine: Yu Han Chen, Jian-An Liao, Shih Lin Lin and Wei Hsun Wang
papers.abstract: This project integrates virtual driving simulation, artificial intelligence (AI), and orthopedic rehabilitation technologies to develop a safe, objective, and quantitative driving ability assessment system. The platform recreates realistic road scenarios, including lane keeping, obstacle avoidance, sudden braking of a leading vehicle, traffic light compliance, and speed limit control. During the simulation, the system continuously collects key driving performance data such as accelerator input, brake pressure, steering wheel angle, vehicle speed, lane deviation, reaction time, and collision events. The primary objective of this research is to evaluate the driving abilities of individuals with knee or hip joint replacements and compare their driving performance with that of healthy drivers. By applying machine learning and AI algorithms to analyze driving behavior patterns, the system establishes driving risk prediction models and high-risk driver classification mechanisms, enabling a more comprehensive understanding of how joint replacement surgery may affect driving safety. Compared with traditional on-road driving tests, the proposed system offers several advantages, including enhanced safety, lower operational costs, repeatable testing conditions, and quantitative data analysis. These features allow researchers and healthcare professionals to conduct objective assessments without exposing participants to real-world traffic risks. The project combines the fields of smart healthcare, orthopedic rehabilitation, artificial intelligence, transportation safety, and aging technology. papers.abstract: Recently, demand has increased for microactuators that serve as precise driving sources in communication and sensing applications. In particular, actuators capable of directly converting electromagnetic-wave energy into mechanical vibration are expected to enable new wireless actuation and sensing platforms. In this study, we propose a novel micro-striped actuator for surface acoustic wave (SAW) excitation based on the spin-current volume effect (SVE). The SVE is a phenomenon in which spin-current injection induces a volume change in magnetostrictive materials [1]. This effect enables compact and precise actuation [2]. The device consists of a Tb20Fe24Co56 magnetostrictive thin film and a Pt thin film fabricated on a silicon-on-insulator (SOI) wafer. In the Pt layer, a spin current is generated from an applied charge current via the spin Hall effect (SHE). Injection of this spin current into the Tb20Fe24Co56 layer induces a volume change. A periodic metallic microstructure is fabricated on the device surface to define high-frequency mechanical vibration modes. In future work, this periodic structure will also serve as a grating for surface plasmon polariton (SPP) excitation, with the aim of converting electromagnetic energy into mechanical vibration through the SVE. As an initial step, the vibration response was evaluated using a laser Doppler vibrometer. Bending vibration modes were observed at approximately 23.75 and 36.71 kHz, providing evidence of SVE-driven mechanical vibration in the fabricated device. References [1] H. papers.abstract: Deep-ultraviolet (DUV) photodetectors have attracted considerable attention because of their potential applications in environmental monitoring, flame sensing, sterilization monitoring, and optical communication. Among ultrawide-bandgap semiconductors, β-Ga2O3 has emerged as a promising material for solar-blind DUV photodetectors owing to its ultrawide bandgap (~4.9eV), excellent thermal stability, and high optical transparency. However, stable p-type β-Ga2O3 remains difficult to achieve; therefore, p-type NiO has been widely employed to construct β-Ga2O3 heterojunction photodetectors [1, 2]. In this work, Li-doped NiO custom-made sputtering targets with different Li concentrations were fabricated using a solid-state reaction process. The effects of Li concentration on the structural, electrical, and optical properties of Li:NiO thin films were systematically investigated to determine the optimum composition of the sputtering target. The optimized Li:NiO thin films were subsequently deposited on Si-doped β-Ga2O3 by RF magnetron sputtering to fabricate the vertical Li:NiO/Si:β-Ga2O3 heterojunction photodetectors. Under 254 nm UV light illumination, the optimized device exhibited a photocurrent of 1.42×10-6 A and a dark current of 1.45×10-10 A at an applied bias of 10 V, corresponding to an ON/OFF current ratio of 10⁴, approximately. In addition, a responsivity of 2.06 A/W was achieved, together with rise and decay times of 9.6 s and 45.6 s, respectively. The excellent rectifying characteristics, low dark current, and enhanced photoresponse indicate that Li concentration engineering effectively improves carrier transport and heterojunction performance. The proposed fabrication strategy provides an effective approach for developing high-performance β-Ga2O3 based solar-blind DUV photodetectors.

papers.abstract: Vascular inflammation is a key pathological process involved in the progression of chronic diseases, including diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular disease, and chronic kidney disease. Spent coffee grounds (SCG), a major by-product of coffee brewing, retain various bioactive compounds, such as polyphenols, chlorogenic acids, and melanoidins, and have attracted increasing attention for their antioxidant and anti-inflammatory potential. However, the vascular protective effects of artificially digested SCG extracts remain largely unexplored. This study aims to establish an in vitro vascular inflammation-on-a-chip platform to evaluate the vascular protective potential of artificially digested SCG extracts under physiologically relevant conditions. Docosahex-aenoic acid (DHA) was used as a positive control. To simulate oral administration, SCG extracts and DHA were subjected to an in vitro gastrointestinal digestion process using simulated salivary fluid (SSF), simulated gastric fluid (SGF), and simulated intestinal fluid (SIF). The digested supernatants were collected for subsequent biological evaluation. To date, SCG extraction, artificial digestion, and preparation of digested samples have been completed. Cytotoxicity assays using human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) demonstrated that treatment with 2% digested samples did not cause apparent cytotoxicity. Therefore, this concentration was selected for subsequent on-chip experiments. Future work will establish a hyperglycemia-induced vascular inflammation model to investigate endothelial integrity, mitochondrial function, and THP-1 monocyte adhesion following treatment with artificially digested SCG extracts. This platform is expected to provide a physiologically relevant approach for evaluating the vascular protective potential of natural bioactive compounds.

papers.abstract: Pain after surgery is still judged mainly from what patients report, a method that provides no continuous signal and breaks down entirely for patients who cannot communicate. Because acute somatic pain following spinal surgery triggers a reproducible autonomic-nervous-system response, the electrocardiogram (ECG) offers a promising physiological channel for a wearable pain-monitoring tool. We built and tested a dual-branch convolutional neural network (CNN) system that both classifies and scores acute postoperative pain from ECG recorded in real surgical patients. Using a self-built wearable device (AD8232 sensor with an ESP32 microcontroller), first validated against a commercial reference monitor, we recorded ECG from 21 spinal-surgery patients at two time points — postoperative day 1 (higher pain, Class 1) and the day before discharge (lower pain, Class 0). From these recordings we extracted 30,750 usable 10-second segments, converted each to a 224×224 grayscale image, and used them to train and test ten ImageNet-pretrained CNN backbones under a strict four-fold leave-patients-out cross-subject protocol. The system produces two complementary outputs: a binary classifier for real-time individual pain-state monitoring, and a regression model estimating group-level Visual Analog Scale (VAS) intensity, useful for evaluating analgesic protocols. Across the four held-out test sets, InceptionV3 achieved the best sensitivity (0.987 ± 0.008), DenseNet121 was perfectly specific in every fold (1.000), and ResNeXt50 gave the lowest regression error (MAE = 0.035). Grad-CAM maps showed activation concentrated over the T wave and QRS complex — regions consistent with a sympathetically driven pain response — supporting the interpretation that the models capture a genuine physiological signature rather than patient-specific artifacts.

Therefore, establishing in vitro models that better reflect the physiological environment of the human body has become a major trend in current cancer research. Compared to traditional two-dimensional (2D) cell culture, three-dimensional (3D) tumor spheres can more realistically simulate interactions between tumor cells and the tumor microenvironment; When combined with Microfluidics technology, it can better simulate the continuous flow of the body, helping to enhance the physiological correlation of drug testing. This study mainly established the A549 three-dimensional microchannel culture platform for non-small cell lung cancer tumor glomeruli and preliminarily evaluated the effects of treatment with Gemcitabine, Metformin, and SW033291 on tumor glomeruli. First, uniformly sized A549 tumor spheres are cultured, then placed into microchannel chips for dynamic drug processing. After drug treatment, in addition to observing the appearance of the tumor glomeruli, sodium dodecylsulfate-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (SDS-PAGE) was used to analyze the expression of total cell proteins. This study has successfully established and maintained the culture of A549 tumor spheres. Under the drug concentrations and treatment times set in this study, no obvious morphological or volumetric changes were observed in the tumor spherical appearance of each group. However, SDS-PAGE analysis revealed significant differences in protein bands after different drug treatments, suggesting that cells may have undergone protein-level molecular reactions even before their appearance changes. In the future, we will further combine proteomics analysis with target protein validation to explore the mechanisms of action of Gemcitabine, Metformin, and SW033291. The goal is to establish a lung cancer drug evaluation platform that closely aligns with human physiological environments, and serve as an important research foundation for future non-animal alternative trials and new drug screening.

By folding thin sheets, a new hexagonal-pyramid origami mechanism is formed, inspired by the Great Pyramid of Giza, Egypt. The mechanism's operating principle has been clearly explained. papers.abstract: Dental caries is among the most prevalent oral diseases worldwide, and early accurate detection is critical for preventing disease progression. Current clinical tools, including visual examination and dental radiography, have limited sensitivity for early lesion detection. Emerging techniques such as fiber-optic transillumination and quantitative laser fluorescence offer certain advantages but are hindered by high cost and limited quantification capability, leaving an unmet need for tools capable of reflecti ng molecular-level changes in enamel [1].Raman spectroscopy has attracted considerable attention in dental hard tissue analysis owing to its non-destructive and highly molecule-specific nature. The characteristic phosphate (PO₄³⁻, ~959 cm⁻¹) signal of hydroxyapatite (HA) in dental enamel decreases upon carious lesion formation, demonstrating its potential as a diagnostic marker [2]. However, due to biological heterogeneity, Raman responses exhibit multi-scale spatial variation between teeth, making absolute signal intensity alone an unreliable diagnostic standard prone to inter-individual misinterpretation. To address this limitation, we developed a portable polarized Raman spectrometer and introduced the depolarization ratio (ρ) as an objective internal reference, calculated from the ratio of Raman intensities under parallel and perpendicular polarization configurations. This parameter reflects the crystallographic orientation anisotropy of HA — sound enamel exhibits low ρ values while demineralized enamel shows elevated ρ. As a ratiometric parameter, ρ is inherently independent of inter-individual signal variation. We systematically established the quantitative relationship between ρ and caries severity, validating the clinical feasibility of a portable polarized Raman system for early dental caries diagnosis.

papers.abstract: Bacterial infections have a continuous dissemination characteristic. Localized infections that are not effectively controlled can progress to bacteremia, potentially leading to septic shock and multiple organ failure. Current clinical diagnosis relies heavily on blood culture methods, with a median time to positivity of approximately 15.7 hours and 85.3% of cases confirmed within 24 hours, delaying treatment and requiring clinicians to administer broad spectrum antibiotics empirically, which may accelerate the development of antimicrobial resistance [1]. Although molecular diagnostics (PCR) and mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF) have shortened identification time, the major limitation of direct MALDI-TOF application to clinical samples lies in the bacterial load present and the detection limit of current protocols, often requiring large sample volumes or culture based enrichment to overcome this constraint, along with high equipment costs and the need for specialized personnel, which together restrict widespread clinical adoption [2]. In this study, we developed an in house optical detection reagent that exhibits distinct colorimetric responses to Gram negative and Gram positive bacteria, enabling preliminary differentiation of bacterial type. Upon contact with bacteria containing blood, the reagent also induces a marked fluorescence signal change, serving as a readout for the presence of bacteria in blood. This approach is expected to enable rapid screening within a few hours, offering a simple and cost effective optical tool for clinical use.

Therefore, the development of highly sensitive and highly selective detection technologies is of great importance for improving early cancer diagnosis and precision medicine. In this study, we successfully synthesized a carbazole-derived fluorescent small molecule, OMP, and established a dual-modal cancer detection platform integrating fluorescence imaging with surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS). The cytotoxicity, intracellular accumulation, fluorescence selectivity, and mitochondrial localization of OMP were systematically evaluated using both cancer and normal cell models. The results demonstrated that treatment with 2 μM OMP for 24 h provided the optimal conditions for fluorescence imaging. OMP exhibited significantly greater fluorescence accumulation in A549 lung cancer cells than in MRC-5 normal lung fibroblasts and showed mitochondrial localization together with dynamic fluorescence redistribution associated with changes in cellular state. To further obtain molecular information from cells, silver nanowires were employed as the SERS substrate, and a 633 nm excitation laser was used for Raman measurements. OMP exhibited three characteristic Raman peaks at approximately 1175, 1315, and 1590 cm⁻¹, which served as a molecular spectral barcode. Combined with intrinsic Raman fingerprints from nucleic acids, proteins, lipids, and cytochrome c, these spectral features enabled effective molecular discrimination between cancer and normal cells. Principal component analysis (PCA) further demonstrated that OMP treatment improved the separation between normal and cancer cells. Overall, the OMP-based fluorescence imaging/SERS platform provides complementary imaging and molecular information for distinguishing cancer cells from normal cells.

papers.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are now pervasive across marine, freshwater, soil, and airborne environments, and their persistence allows them to accumulate through the food chain and ultimately reach humans, raising ecological and public health concerns. In this work, fluorescent probes exhibiting Twisted Intramolecular Charge Transfer (TICT) behavior were applied to develop a fast microplastic detection strategy. Because TICT-active molecules are highly sensitive to shifts in local polarity and viscosity, their conformational and excited-state dynamics change upon contact with different plastic surfaces, producing distinguishable fluorescence signatures. This sensitivity, combined with rapid response and simple operation, makes such probes well-suited for preliminary microplastic identification in complex samples and as a pre-screening tool ahead of detailed analysis. This study systematically examined the fluorescence response of TICT-based probes toward common microplastic types, comparing signal variation and discriminative power across polymer surfaces, with the aim of establishing a sensitive, high-throughput screening method for future microplastic monitoring applications.

However, SERS has long faced a fundamental trade off between sensitivity and reproducibility; with continued advances in nanotechnology, the scope of SERS applications has expanded significantly, establishing it as a prominent research field spanning chemistry, physics, materials science, and biomedicine, while its performance still holds considerable room for optimization—an opportunity that continues to drive progress in SERS substrate design [2]. In this study, silver nanowires were used to investigate the enhancement of SERS performance via the silicon-based coffee-ring effect. Unconfined silicon wafers demonstrated good multi-analyte reusability, though spatial uniformity remained limited. Targeted measurements at the co-localized region of the dual coffee-ring effect—formed by both silver nanowires and the analyte—revealed a substantial local signal enhancement compared to the droplet center region. papers.abstract: Micro-aerial vehicles (MAVs) and other unmanned autonomous systems require path planners that balance route quality, replanning latency, and limited onboard memory. This paper presents a controlled comparison of A*, Jump Point Search (JPS), and D* Lite on 8-connected occupancy grids with cardinal and diagonal costs of 10 and 14. The desktop benchmark uses 100 independent solvable random-map instances per size–density configuration and 20 timing repetitions per instance. It also evaluates 100 start–goal pairs on each of two structured Moving AI Lab maps. JPS consistently reduces runtime and expanded-node counts relative to A*, whereas D* Lite depends strongly on update mode and map structure. On the structured maps, a path-blocking protocol produces 100 valid events for a rooms map but no valid event for a maze map because every attempted update makes the updated instance unreachable. An ESP32 validation without external PSRAM shows that JPS is fastest for the tested initial-planning cases. D* Lite has a lower median repair latency than A* and JPS on the tested 50×50 dynamic case, but is slower than both baselines on the tested 100 × 100 case. All tested 500 × 500 cases are safely rejected during grid allocation because of insufficient heap. The results characterize how map structure, update mode, and implementation-level memory behavior affect classical grid planners on a resource-constrained microcontroller.

papers.abstract: Photoelasticity provides full-field visualization of stress-related fringes; however, quantitative and inverse analyses require controlled optical conditions, expert interpretation, and repeated finite element method (FEM) simulations. This study proposes a physics-guided bidirectional framework linking loads, stress fields, and photoelastic fringes. FEM calculates displacement and stress in polymethyl methacrylate disks and rings under uniaxial, biaxial, and eccentric loads, from which isochromatic fringes are generated using the stress-optic law. A PointNet-based physics-informed neural network (PINN) approximates displacement fields subject to equilibrium, constitutive, and boundary constraints, while CycleGAN translates between unpaired isochromatic and isoclinic domains. For inverse analysis, a convolutional neural network estimates load magnitude and position from fringe images. The predicted loads are fed back into the forward model to regenerate fringes for consistency checking. Simulations show spatial agreement between stress concentrations and fringe density, while predicted loads follow ground-truth trends under symmetric and asymmetric loading. In a representative case, PINN inference reduces solution time from 82.4 to 5.7 s (93%). Optical-noise augmentation further tests robustness under experiment-like conditions. These results demonstrate rapid, closed-loop load reconstruction and support future experimental applications to miniature mechanical components.

papers.abstract: This paper addresses the development and validation of a comprehensive mathematical model for a novel Tracked Hybrid Drone architecture capable of seamlessly executing both aerial flight and terrestrial locomotion. The proposed system integrates a traditional quad-rotor configuration for multi-rotor flight with an advanced continuous tracked-wheel subsystem tailored for rugged ground mobility. Utilizing the Euler–Lagrange approach, separate dynamic and kinematic equations are formulated for the aerial and ground operation phases, incorporating distinct non-holonomic constraints, surface-interaction forces, and actuator configurations intrinsic to each mode. Furthermore, a unified switching logic and wrench-blending framework, coupled with a multi-point compliant ground interaction model, is introduced to govern cross-domain state transitions and mitigate mechanical impact disturbances. High-fidelity numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed mathematical model accurately captures the highly non-linear, coupled hybrid dynamics of the vehicle. Evaluated via rigorous integral criteria and error-tracking metrics, the system exhibits asymptotic tracking performance during aerial maneuvers and maintains absolute structural stability during touchdown and terrestrial differential navigation. Ultimately, this mathematical framework provides a robust theoretical foundation for subsequent advanced control system synthesis, multi-mode trajectory optimization, and hardware-in-the-loop validation of tracked hybrid unmanned systems deployed in complex, unstructured environments.

papers.abstract: This paper investigates the sliding wear behaviour of a three-dimensional ball-on-disc contact using finite element analysis. The study focuses on the influence of evolving contact geometry on wear-volume prediction and evaluates a Lewis-inspired area correction combined with Archard’s wear law. A threedimensional Abaqus model was developed for a ball-on-disc configuration subjected to a normal load of 10 N and a sliding distance of 0.250 mm under frictionless contact. Local wear evolution was implemented through the UMESHMOTION subroutine using the Archard wear formulation. Based purely on the Abaqus simulation data, the study comparatively evaluates the conventional Archard’s law model and the Lewis model formulation. Preliminary numerical findings indicate that the conventional Archard’s law formulation yields a simulated wear volume of 3.11x10−7 mm³ and a maximum wear depth of 0.05482 μm. This reveals a difference of approximately 10.85% in the predicted wear volume between the two models, highlighting the sensitivity of wear simulations to evolving contact geometry. These results constitute a purely numerical comparison. Further mesh-sensitivity analysis and experimental validation are required to determine which formulation better represents physical wear behaviour.

papers.abstract: This study investigates the thermomechanical response of an all-ceramic zirconia dental bridge under combined masticatory loading and oral temperature variations. A three-dimensional finite element model of the dental bridge was developed and analysed using ANSYS Workbench. Mechanical, thermal, and coupled thermomechanical analyses were conducted to evaluate the distributions of stress and deformation within the bridge structure. Particular attention was given to the connector and supporting regions, where stress concentrations may influence structural performance. The results show that temperature variations alter the stress distribution and modify the critical stress regions compared with mechanical loading alone. Under coupled thermomechanical conditions, the critical stress concentration was located at the gingival aspect of the connector between the pontic and the abutment. This finding indicates that the pontic–abutment transition is particularly sensitive to combined mechanical and thermal loading. Therefore, thermal effects should be considered when evaluating zirconia dental bridges and optimizing connector geometry.

papers.abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) have emerged as a promising approach for energy-efficient Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems due to their event-driven processing mechanism. This paper presents the design and implementation of a SoC-FPGA-based SNN for multi-class driver drowsiness classification. An Artificial Neural Network (ANN) with a 576-128-4 architecture was first trained and then converted into an SNN model using Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) neurons and Rate Coding. The SNN architecture is implemented in SystemVerilog and integrated into the Cyclone V SoC DE10-Standard through the Avalon-MM interface. The proposed system classifies four driver states: Awake, Fatigue, Drowsy, and Severe Drowsy. Experimental results show that the ANN model achieved an overall classification accuracy of 96.02% on the test dataset, while the FPGA-based SNN model achieved an overall accuracy of 84.54%. The inference time of the SNN core on the FPGA ranges from 144.8 ms to 199.1 ms. The implemented system operates at approximately 10 frames per second (FPS) for driver-state recognition. These results demonstrate the feasibility of deploying ANN-to-SNN conversion and SNN inference on SoC-FPGA platforms for embedded and edge AI applications.

papers.abstract: Whether a polycrystal breaks along its grain boundaries or through its grains is set by the strength of those boundaries relative to the grain interiors, and peridynamics computes that competition without a rule for where a crack may go. An ordinary state-based peridynamic model for cubic crystals is applied here to polycrystalline silicon under rapid tension. A square plate with two edge notches and one hundred randomly oriented grains is pulled apart until it separates. The critical energy release rate is taken from published recommended values for the three cleavage planes, each run at three grain-boundary coefficients. The share of broken bonds crossing a boundary falls monotonically as the boundaries are strengthened, reproducing the intergranular to transgranular transition. The three toughness values leave that ordering untouched, which is shown to be a similarity of the formulation under the chosen loading rather than a property of the material. Removing the similarity recovers a difference of nearly three percentage points. Four discretizations and ten microstructure realisations separate the numerical from the statistical scatter.

papers.abstract: Atherosclerosis is a chronic cardiovascular disease that can cause vascular lumen obstruction, leading to acute coronary syndrome, myocardial infarction, or stroke. Current atherosclerosis imaging methods are limited by cost, complexity, radiation exposure, invasiveness, and suitability for routine screening. Therefore, this study proposes a simulation-based carotid artery model to assess plaque detection using electrical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). The effects of electrode radii and inter-electrode spacing on plaque-size discrimination were also evaluated. The model employs a four-electrode measurement configuration over a frequency range from 1 Hz to 50 kHz. The model was evaluated using three electrode radii r_e, eight edge-to edge inter-electrode spacings a, five plaque radii ra, and one no-plaque reference condition, resulting in 3 × 8 × 6 = 144 simulations. The impedance response was evaluated using the Nyquist-derived tangent angle α, RMSE, and sensitivity analysis. Based on the combined evaluation of the tangent angle α and RMSE, the configuration with re = 0.15 cm and a = 0.7 cm provided the most balanced performance. This configuration exhibited a stable increasing trend with plaque radius, high linearity (R² = 0.893), and a stable angle response (σ_∆α = 0.074), thereby supporting the feasibility of plaque-size detection. These preliminary numerical results support the feasibility of impedance-based plaque-size detection and highlight the importance of electrode-geometry optimization.

papers.abstract: Radiofrequency ablation (RFA) outcomes depend on both applicator configuration and tumor geometry, particularly when part of the target extends away from the main electrode trajectory. This study investigated the influence of active-electrode length on thermal-damage coverage of compact breast tumors and tumors with idealized lateral extensions using a three-dimensional computational model. An obliquely inserted RFA applicator was modeled by coupling stationary electric-current conduction, Joule heating, transient Pennes bioheat transfer, and Arrhenius thermal-damage analysis. Three active-electrode lengths (L_act = 10, 14, and 18 mm) were combined with tumor-extension lengths of L_ext = 0, 4, and 8 mm at V_app = 17.5 V for 120 s. Increasing Lact increased integrated Joule power but reduced both peak tumor temperature and volumetric damage coverage. For the compact tumor, C_99 decreased from 12.17% at L_act = 10 mm to 7.56% and 2.90% at 14 and 18 mm, respectively. For tumors with extensions, no extension region reached either α ≥ 0.632 or α ≥ 0.99 in any configuration. Meanwhile, the healthy-tissue volume reaching α ≥ 0.632 increased markedly with L_act, whereas V_{healthy,99} remained negligible. These results indicate that peak temperature or total Joule power alone is insufficient to characterize RFA response. Under the investigated conditions, increasing active electrode length did not improve tumor coverage and was insufficient to treat off-axis tumor extensions, highlighting the importance of volumetric damage metrics and applicator–target spatial alignment.

papers.abstract: Energy demand in a convergecast wireless rechargeable sensor network is structurally uneven: nodes near the base station relay for everyone behind them and drain fastest, while distant nodes cost a charger the most to reach. Chargers scheduled independently over the field therefore spend much of their budget on repeated long return trips. We present DTSC, which cuts the field into angular sectors of balanced consumption and assigns each to an inner-outer charger pair. The outer charger never returns to the base station; the inner charger refuels there and transfers energy at a rendezvous point, so the long return leg is paid once per pair rather than once per charger. Across 12,500 simulations DTSC matches three of four baselines on dead nodes at the heaviest load while travelling 46-62% less, a margin holding at every quantile; the fourth travels less still but loses four times as many nodes.

papers.abstract: Millimeter-wave vehicular links require rapid beam reconfiguration to maintain connectivity under high mobility, blockage, and frequent LOS/NLOS transitions. In this work, we propose a mobility-aware 3D hybrid beamforming scheme that employs an artificial bee colony (ABC) strategy to adaptively configure beams in dynamic vehicular networks. The proposed scheme jointly determines the azimuth and elevation beam directions and transmit power while accounting for mobility-induced channel variations. A dual-array fluid antenna system (FAS) provides additional spatial flexibility for rapid beam reconfiguration, while a Hamming window is employed to control sidelobes and mitigate inter-beam interference. The framework further incorporates LOS/NLOS-aware beam selection, hysteresis-based switching, and adaptive power control to maintain stable links and limit unnecessary energy consumption. Simulation results demonstrate improved signal quality, spectral efficiency (SE), and throughput, together with lower energy consumption, path loss, outage rate (OR), and beam realignment latency (BRL) compared with traditional and existing metaheuristic approaches.

papers.abstract: Abnormal vehicle behavior, sudden traffic slowdowns, and unexpected roadway events can propagate rapidly through connected transportation systems. To address this problem, we propose a temporal multi-feature anomaly (TMFA) detection method for identifying abnormal traffic behavior from video. The proposed method extracts vehicle trajectories and jointly models speed variation, movement direction, spatial distribution, traffic occupancy, and temporal changes in motion to characterize evolving traffic conditions. These features are integrated into a multi-feature anomaly score, which is then temporally smoothed to improve anomaly consistency and suppress transient detection fluctuations. Detected anomalies can subsequently trigger early warning messages within vehicular communication networks. Experiments on real-world traffic video evaluate anomaly detection performance under varying traffic conditions. As summarized in Table I, the proposed TMFA achieves a 3.23% anomaly rate, 225 anomalous frames, and a mean anomaly-event duration of 0.096 s, demonstrating effective and temporally consistent identification of abnormal traffic events for proactive traffic safety.

papers.abstract: Reliable and efficient vehicle clustering is essential for maintaining scalable and stable communication in highly dynamic vehicular networks. Dynamic vehicle distributions and mobility variations make fixed clustering strategies inefficient for vehicular networks. To address this issue, we propose vehicle-group adaptive clustering (VGAC), a traffic-aware framework that dynamically adapts vehicle groups to changing roadway conditions obtained from traffic video. VGAC jointly considers vehicle density, spatial occupancy, local concentration, mobility, and directional consistency to estimate the traffic state and adjust the communication range accordingly. Cluster heads (CHs) are selected based on connectivity, mobility stability, and spatial centrality, while temporal hysteresis reduces unnecessary range changes and cluster restructuring caused by short-term fluctuations. Unlike fixed-range, distance-based, and density-based approaches, VGAC integrates spatial and temporal traffic characteristics into cluster formation and maintenance. Experiments on real-world traffic videos evaluate cluster size, stability, CHs changes, re-clustering rate, and communication overhead. Results demonstrate that VGAC forms larger vehicle groups while reducing cluster restructuring and communication overhead under dynamic traffic conditions.

papers.abstract: This work presents a dual-axis symmetric magnetic sensor fabricated using a 0.18-μm CMOS process. N-type sensing regions are formed in a P-type substrate, and the Hall sensing electrodes are operated under a slight reverse-bias condition to generate depletion regions that guide carrier transport toward deeper substrate regions. When an external magnetic field is applied, carriers are vertically deflected by the Lorentz force, producing charge separation and a Hall electric field. Magnetic-field sensing is achieved from the differential voltage between the Hall sensing electrodes. Current confinement electrodes suppress current spreading and reduce leakage current, while current injection electrodes provide the driving current. Measurements show that increasing the Hall sensing bias improves sensitivity by establishing a sufficient depletion region. In contrast, excessive current injection bias reduces sensitivity because of changes in the electric-field distribution and carrier transport path. The proposed sensor achieves a sensitivity of 170.72 V/AT with a power consumption of 0.805 mW, verifying the feasibility of the proposed reverse-biased sensing structure.

papers.abstract: Multi-charger scheduling in wireless rechargeable sensor networks must weigh sensor death risk, charger energy, travel cost, return-to-base feasibility and inter-charger coordination at once, and schedulers driven by local urgency alone duplicate service and leave whole regions unattended. We present HQARRF, a two-level scheduler. Below, an interpretable ARR-F score ranks candidate clusters through an attraction term for local urgency, a repulsion term against charger crowding and a force bonus from nearby critical sensors. Above, adaptive zones compress regional state into a deadline-based risk estimate, and a gated Q-learning controller decides only whether to redirect service to a high-risk, under-served zone. Over 27 parameter points HQARRF attains the highest mean survival rate at 26, improving survival by 20.7 percentage points over the mean of five baselines and 9.2 over the strongest baseline at each point. An ablation isolates the upper level: its gain tracks how often the controller fires.

papers.abstract: On-demand charging lets a sensor request service once its energy falls below a threshold theta. Nearly all schemes fix one theta network-wide, which ignores how unevenly relay load falls across clusters: set it high and the charger queue saturates, set it low and nodes die before service arrives. We add two cooperating deep reinforcement learning agents to a conventional clustering-and-routing stack. A threshold agent resets theta per cluster every 60 seconds from recent request history; a route agent decides at departure whether to detour to a critical cluster en route. Over 12 matched energy seeds at each of five network sizes the framework beats the fixed-threshold scheme it builds on by 2.6 to 14.2 percentage points. More telling than the means is the spread: at 200 sensors the fixed threshold collapses on 8 of 32 runs, once to 9% survival, while the adaptive threshold never falls below 86.3%.

papers.abstract: Under dense deployment a ground wireless charging vehicle (WCV) is too slow to meet every sensor deadline, while a purely aerial charger is capped by its battery. Existing hybrid schemes fall back from Nearest Job First to Earliest Deadline First only once the former is declared infeasible, so nodes due inside that switch window are already lost. We present CHASE, which applies both rules inside every WCV leg: it anchors the most urgent target by deadline, then folds in only the pending nodes lying within a narrow corridor along that leg. A second mechanism recovers a UAV launched from a moving WCV by solving the rendezvous with a provably contractive fixed-point iteration. Over 30 seeds CHASE sustains 82.8% survival at 1000 nodes against 74.8% for CHCS, peaking at a 10.0-point margin; removing the corridor alone costs 19.8 points.

papers.abstract: Measuring radial runout is an essential geometric inspection requirement for transmission parts in precision mechanical machining. However, traditional contact measurement methods often easily affect the component surface, are slow in speed, and depend greatly on operator skills, while imported non-contact measuring devices are overly expensive. To solve this problem, this research paper presents a design and fabrication scheme for an automatic, non-contact radial runout measurement system applying a point laser displacement sensor, targeting inspection objects that are stepped cylindrical parts with diameters from Ø10mm to Ø30mm and a maximum length of 200mm. The proposed system uses a microstepping transmission mechanism closely synchronized with a high-speed AD7606 data acquisition module to record and accurately reconstruct the 2D profile of the part in real-time. Comparative experimental results show that the system operates stably with very small absolute errors compared to the traditional dial indicator measurement method, achieving errors of 0.01613 mm and 0.01894 mm at steps 2 and 3 of a stepped part (equivalent to relative errors of 8.135% and 13.44%). This solution not only completely eliminates operational technique errors in traditional methods, but also proves great potential in applying quality control at small and medium enterprises, as well as effectively serving research and technical training work.

papers.abstract: As network applications face increasing performance demands, efficient server-side data transfer has become critical. Although the Linux network stack provides stability and compatibility, frequent context switches and data copies between kernel and user space can limit performance. Kernel-bypass frameworks such as F-Stack and Z-Stack reduce these overheads through user-space packet processing. This study compares Linux, F-Stack, and Z-Stack in a file server application using two multicore coordination models: centralized and decentralized. File servers were implemented with each network stack under both models and evaluated using the wrk benchmark. The results show that F-Stack and Z-Stack significantly outperform Linux under high concurrency. Z-Stack generally achieves higher throughput and lower latency than F-Stack, mainly due to zero-copy and more effective multicore utilization. At extremely high concurrency, the decentralized model provides more stable latency by allowing each core to handle connections independently, whereas the centralized model maintains high throughput under low-to-moderate loads by separating connection acceptance from I/O processing. Under lighter workloads, Linux retains advantages in stability and maintainability.These findings provide practical guidance for selecting network stacks and multicore architectures for high-performance file servers.

A coupled-field finite-element model was developed in ANSYS, incorporating the actual wheel-rim geometry through a Remote Point and Remote Displacement representation to preserve rim–harvester load transfer while reducing computational cost. The prestressed harmonic analysis used a structural loss factor ηₛ = 0.02 (ζ = 1%) and evaluated frame stress, voltage, and mean load power from 10 to 1000 Hz for variations in resistance, wheel speed, and proof mass. A resonance near 460 Hz under the imposed harmonic excitation produced a maximum simulated mean power of 16.748 W for 10 kΩ, but the associated frame stress exceeded the assumed 250 MPa steel-yield threshold; therefore, the resonant result is not a physically admissible elastic design point. At 10 Hz, representative powers were only 0.551-5.51 μW. The results suggest potential for trickle charging or highly duty-cycled TPMS operation with storage and power conditioning, while continuous self-powered operation is not yet demonstrated. Full-harvester experimental validation and identification of the effective system damping remain necessary.

However, the impedance of subject skin and skull tissue frequently varies significantly between 1 kΩ and 10 kΩ due to individual differences or electrode contact conditions. If conventional current sources fail to maintain a constant current under such high-impedance loads, it not only compromises experimental repeatability but may also induce skin burns or discomfort caused by localized high electric field intensity. To address these limitations, this study proposes a feasible hardware solution.

papers.abstract: Ultrasonic-assisted turning (UAT) requires an ultrasonic vibration system capable of maintaining stable resonance and delivering sufficient vibration am-plitude to the cutting tool. Therefore, the performance of the ultrasonic horn crucial role in the efficiency and reliability of the machining system. This study presents the numerical design and experimental validation of a piezoelectric ultrasonic transducer–horn assembly developed for ultrasonic-assisted turning. An electromechanical finite-element model is established to predict the resonance characteristics and vibration response of the proposed system. The model combine the piezoelectric, horn, cutting tool, bolt pretension, and threaded contact in order to represent the mechanical and electromechanical behavior of the actual assembly. Frequency domain analyses are performed to determine the resonance frequency, electrical impedance response, vibration mode, and displacement distribution along the horn and the cutting tool. Based on the numerical results, the horn geometry is designed and fabricated. The experiment was conducted using electrical impedance measurements and vibration response tests. The experimentally obtained resonance characteristics are compared with the numerical predictions to assess the accuracy of the proposed model. The results demonstrate that the developed finite-element approach can effectively predict the electromechanical response of the ultrasonic horn and provide a practical basis for the design and optimization of ultrasonic vibration systems for UAT applications

papers.abstract: Assessing tea flavor intensity today still relies on manual sensory cupping or chemical assays—accurate, but slow, costly, and hard to scale—while real-time electronic alternatives require individually coating a new sensor chip for every measurement. Tea’s sensory quality depends on Relative Tea Concentration Indicators and flavor intensity, to which theanine contributes the core "sweet aftertaste," and Extended-gate field-effect transistor (EGFET) sensors are a promising real-time platform for evaluating it — but only once each chip carries a resource-intensive, inconsistency-prone hydrothermal coating (e.g., Ga₂O₃@5%Sn). To remove this per-chip coating requirement, we propose AE-FuzzyNN, a virtual sensing framework that acts as a soft-ware-defined amplifier, reconstructing high-gain signals from a bare Gold (Au) electrode’s raw electrical response, validated against dilution-ratio-based flavor-intensity proxies rather than absolute theanine concentration. An Autoencoder (AE) compresses the 51-dimensional signal into a latent space tractable for fuzzy rule construction; a Fuzzy Neural Network (FNN) with Gaussian membership functions then maps the non-linear bare-to-coated transfer function, reproducing at the signal level the sensitivity gain the physical coating would otherwise provide. Under 15-fold LOOCV, the framework achieves a reconstruction RMSE of 0.255 ± 0.129 mA, and the virtual sensor yields a sensitivity of 94.9 uA/a.u. — a 101.3% recovery of the physically coated chip’s sensitivity (93.7 uA/a.u.) — with a stable R² of 0.9191. Once trained, the framework delivers this performance at near-zero marginal cost, a favorable trade-off against a modest linearity loss.

papers.abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) devices have been increasingly deployed in applications such as smart manufacturing, smart cities, and environmental monitoring. These devices generate large amounts of diverse data that can be utilized by machine learning (ML) to enhance the sensing, prediction, and decision-making capabilities of IoT systems. However, centralizing IoT data on cloud servers for model training may raise privacy concerns and introduce considerable communication overhead. Federated learning (FL) provides an alternative paradigm that enables distributed IoT devices to collaboratively train ML models while keeping their private data locally. By exchanging model updates instead of raw data, FL reduces the need for centralized data transmission while preserving data locality. A key challenge to FL over IoT devices is the heterogeneous IoT environment, where different devices may have significantly different computing and communication capabilities. Such heterogeneity may lead to inefficient model assignment from the FL server, as a uniform model may not be suitable for devices with different resource constraints. Model compression methods such as model pruning can help adapt the model complexity to match the training capabilities of individual devices. For example, resource-constrained devices can be assigned smaller or lower-precision models, while more capable devices can train models with higher computational complexity. However, algorithm-level reduction in model complexity may not be fully translated into actual computational savings on hardware devices. For example, model pruning commonly removes less important weights by setting them to zero, but conventional hardware and dense computation libraries may still perform the corresponding multiply-accumulate operations without effectively exploiting the resulting sparsity. Consequently, many existing hardware platforms and machine-learning implementations may not efficiently benefit from such heterogeneous model configurations. This research proposes the idea of using FPGA-based platforms to represent heterogeneous IoT devices for implementing FL systems. By exploiting the hardware reconfigurability of FPGAs, model pruning can potentially be translated into lower hardware-level computational complexity, thereby reducing the training burden on resource-constrained devices. The goal of this research is to investigate the relationship among IoT device resources, FL model configurations, and FPGA hardware implementations, and further consider the feasibility of FPGAs in resource-aware FL environments. The proposed concept can be further investigated by analyzing model accuracy, computing and communication overhead, and FPGA hardware resource utilization.

papers.title: Exploring Group-Based Device Collaboration for Federated Learning over Heterogeneous IoT Devices

authors.name: Huai-An Su
affiliations: National Chung Hsing University

papers.authorsLine: Huai-An Su1
affiliations: National Chung Hsing University
papers.abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) systems consist of numerous sensors and computing devices that collect and generate data from real-world environments. With machine learning being integrated into IoT applications, devices are required to perform not only sensing and data collection but also distributed model training. Federated learning (FL) enables IoT devices to collaboratively train models without sharing raw data. However, the different computing capabilities and communication conditions among client devices may result in straggler issues. Such stragglers may become the bottleneck of synchronous FL training, increasing the overall training delay. Our previous work proposed Device-to-Device Assisted Federated Learning (DAFL) [1], which utilizes D2D communication between device pairs, where fast-performing devices (helpers) help slow-performing devices (stragglers) reduce the training delay caused by device heterogeneity. DAFL assigns each pair of devices as a collaboration unit while using split learning (SL) to partition the straggler’s local model. However, pair-based collaboration limits the assisting resources available to each device. Moreover, when the number and distribution of helpers and stragglers are imbalanced, some devices may struggle to find suitable collaboration partners. This research explores group-based device collaboration for FL over heterogeneous IoT environments. Unlike the one-to-one pairing in DAFL, we consider grouping multiple IoT devices with different capabilities. The stragglers may better utilize the computing and communication resources available within their groups. Such a framework provides greater flexibility in resource utilization and reduces the dependency on a single assisting device. To support the new group-based collaboration, the existing SL technique designed for device pairs requires further extension. Models from stragglers can be split into multiple model segments and assigned to different helpers within the group, so that the local training workload can be processed by multiple helpers. This research uses the group-based collaborative FL framework as a foundation to investigate device grouping, model partitioning, and heterogeneous resource allocation across IoT devices. We further investigate its potential to reduce the overall FL training delay. [1] H.-a. Su, P. Prakash, R. Chen, et al., “DAFL: Device-to-Device Transmissions for Delay-Efficient Federated Learning Over Mobile Devices,” IEEE Internet of Things Journal, vol. 12, no. 6, 2025.

papers.abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) communication can provide high data rates for V2X networks, but high vehicle mobility makes reliable beam tracking and beam management challenging. Directional beamforming becomes particularly challenging when a single transmission must serve multiple vehicles with different positions and channel conditions. To address this challenge, we propose a predictive particle swarm optimization (P-PSO)-based multicast beamforming method for mmWave V2X networks. The proposed method uses vehicle mobility and spatial information to form multicast groups and predict their spatial evolution, while a group-aware P-PSO mechanism optimizes the beam direction for multiple receivers. The optimization considers the weakest receiver in each multicast group to improve group-level reliability. Unlike fixed-beam and purely reactive multicast schemes, P-PSO proactively adapts the beam configuration to vehicle mobility and group geometry. Simulation results show that the proposed approach outperforms benchmark methods.

papers.abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks require efficient beamforming to maintain reliable links under rapid satellite motion, varying inter-satellite distances, and frequent beam misalignment [1] [2]. However, fixed-beam and distance-based schemes offer limited adaptability, whereas instantaneous received-power selection can lead to frequent beam changes and high management overhead. To address these limitations, we propose topology-aware adaptive beamforming (TAAB) for dynamic LEO satellite networks. TAAB uses satellite position, link distance, propagation delay, and geometric azimuth and elevation angles to identify suitable beam directions. A joint selection metric combines beamforming gain, angular alignment, beam stability, and switching cost. In addition, an adaptive update rule retains the current beam when a new beam provides insufficient improvement, which reduces unnecessary beam changes. The method is evaluated with real satellite link and position datasets against benchmark schemes. Results show that TAAB improves effective link performance while substantially reducing beam-management overhead, which illustrates its suitability for dynamic LEO satellite networks.
