papers.abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) communication can provide data rates up to 10 Gbps, making it suitable for the stringent throughput and latency requirements of vehicle-to-everything (V2X) networks. However, highly directional mmWave links are sensitive to blockage, and conventional exhaustive beam sweeping causes high signaling and computational overhead. To address this issue, we propose a federated learning (FL)-based connection-angle prediction model that predicts optimal azimuth and elevation angles three seconds ahead using only local vehicle states, without sharing raw trajectory data. A residual gated recurrent unit (GRU) predicts the angular deviation from the current pointing angle using a one-second sequence of ten sampled frames. Vehicles collaboratively train the model using federated averaging (FedAvg) by exchanging only model weights. The proposed method achieves an azimuth mean absolute error of 0.64° and a 5° beam-alignment rate of 97.7%, outperforming benchmark methods. It also maintains over 90% alignment under sparse traffic.

papers.abstract: LoRaWAN relies on randomized transmission delays to avoid repeated collisions on channels. However, compromised or malicious devices can exploit this by transmitting at fixed, bursty, or too short intervals. To address this threat, we propose a two-stage defense framework that includes a network-server detection engine based on statistical randomness tests and normalized Shannon entropy. Upon detecting an attack, the system activates a lightweight Slotted ALOHA mitigation scheme, in which an authenticated downlink beacon broadcasts a shared seed for synchronized time-slot selection. A physical-layer LoRaWAN simulator is used to evaluate the framework, which effectively detects malicious backoff behaviors and mitigates collision performance loss.

papers.abstract: The rapid growth of IoT applications makes LoRaWAN networks vulnerable to security threats due to their open and heterogeneous nature. While federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without sharing raw data, single-stage FL models often struggle to capture diverse security patterns across heterogeneous devices. To address this, we propose a two-stage FL framework combining a primary model (SASN) with a residual refinement model (FRAN). In the first stage, clients collaboratively train the SASN model; the uncaptured residual information is then extracted and used by FRAN for second-stage learning. Evaluated on real LoRaWAN data, the SASN–FRAN framework achieves progressive security representation refinement while preserving data privacy.

papers.abstract: Objectives: This study investigates the potential anti-cancer efficacy and molecular mechanisms of spent coffee grounds (SCG) extracts in the breast tumor microenvironment. While massive SCG disposal (40-50% of coffee chain waste) generates toxic, water-polluting leachate, its richness in anti-inflammatory and antioxidant bioactive compounds offers great potential for functional food development. Targeting the high-inflammation and high-oxidative stress characteristics of the tumor microenvironment is key to suppressing tumor progression. Methodology: Active-rich SCG samples from various bean sources were screened and subjected to microwave-assisted extraction (MAE) to break tough cell walls and retrieve polyphenols. The extracts underwent simulated gastrointestinal digestion to obtain metabolic variants. These were introduced into a microfluidic 3D breast tumor microenvironment model—comprising breast cancer spheroids, human endothelial cells, and monocyte-derived macrophages—to analyze spheroid volume changes and cellular molecular interactions, using Doxorubicin as a control. Expected Outcomes: This research aims to promote a circular economy and advance natural-product tumor inhibition mechanisms. We developed a 3D microfluidic breast cancer model as a high-resolution, biomimetic platform to visualize SCG's impact on angiogenesis inhibition and immune regulation, providing an advanced alternative for in vivo studies. Specific SCG digested extracts are expected to effectively inhibit spheroid growth and modulate microenvironmental inflammation and oxidative stress. Conclusion: This project bridges food waste valorization with advanced 3D microfluidic oncology modeling. It opens sustainable pathways for eco-friendly recycling and establishes a clinically relevant platform for screening natural anti-cancer compounds.

papers.abstract: Pseudogenes have emerged as important regulators in cancer biology, yet their roles within synthetic lethality (SL) networks remain largely unexplored. We developed an integrative computational workflow that combines SynLethDB 2.0 with The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) RNA-sequencing and overall-survival data to identify and prioritize pseudogene-associated SL interactions. SL records containing at least one pseudogene were quality controlled, mapped to six TCGA cohorts, and evaluated by DESeq2-based tumor–normal differential expression and quartile-based Kaplan–Meier analysis. Twenty-four cancer-specific SL records were identified, comprising five pseudogenes and 15 unique pseudogene–partner relationships. RAS-family genes (HRAS, KRAS, NRAS) accounted for 18 of 24 records (75.0%) and 9 of the 15 unique relationships, indicating a prominent RAS-associated interaction pattern. OFCC1 was strongly upregulated in LUAD, COAD, and LIHC (log2 fold change 3.36–4.39) and was prognostic in all three cohorts. MROH5 showed the strongest survival association in KIRC (log-rank P = 0.0013), whereas SLC66A1L displayed opposite expression and prognostic directions in LIHC and KICH. NAT8B–FBXW7 was the only low-throughput-supported pair and had the highest SynLethDB score. Three of the eight pseudogene-cancer survival associations (MROH5 in KIRC, OFCC1 in LIHC, SLC66A1L in LIHC) remained significant after Benjamini–Hochberg correction. These results define a compact, cancer-context-dependent landscape of pseudogene-mediated SL and prioritize OFCC1, MROH5, SLC66A1L, C19orf48, and NAT8B for experimental validation. Our study provides the first systematic pan-cancer characterization of pseudogene-mediated SL networks and highlights novel prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic candidates for precision oncology.

papers.abstract: Chronic stress dysregulates the hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal (HPA) axis and is a well-established risk factor for cardiovascular, metabolic and mental-health disorders, yet objective, continuous stress assessment remains clinically difficult. Cortisol, the principal glucocorticoid biomarker of HPA-axis activity, is present in sweat at levels tracking blood concentrations, making sweat an attractive biofluid for wearable monitoring via label-free, low-cost electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). However, most EIS-based sweat-cortisol sensors require antibody or aptamer functionalization to reach adequate sensitivity and selectivity. This study evaluates whether a bare, label-free gold interdigitated electrode (IDE-Au) can precisely and repeatably detect and quantify cortisol using frequency-domain signal processing alone. Matrix-matched cortisol standards (0–100 ng/mL) in artificial sweat were measured by broadband EIS (10 Hz–50 MHz) on MicruX ED-IDE3-Au electrodes. The raw susceptance response at 836 kHz showed a statistically confirmed, concentration-ordered trend across all six groups (Page’s L = 417, p = 0.002), establishing that a genuine concentration-dependent electrical response is present before any feature engineering. Building on this foundation, a dual-frequency, self-normalized feature log₁₀|Z(8.92 kHz)/Im(11.25 kHz)| increased approximately linearly with cortisol concentration across the five cortisol-containing groups (R² = 0.942). Using an independently optimized frequency-difference feature [Im(Z)(37.868 MHz) − Im(Z)(357.4 kHz)], cortisol was discriminated from matrix-blank controls with high statistical confidence (p < 0.0001). The same dual-frequency feature also showed high measurement repeatability across all concentrations (relative standard deviation ≤ 0.44%). These results demonstrate that a bare-electrode EIS platform can precisely and repeatably quantify and discriminate cortisol in an artificial-sweat matrix without a recognition layer. These features were selected from the same dataset used to evaluate them, so independent validation on a separate dataset and in real human sweat is needed before translation to a practical, low-cost, label-free wearable stress-monitoring tool.

papers.abstract: Boron is a critical water-quality parameter for reclaimed water used in semiconductor manufacturing, where concentrations below 0.1 mg/L are required. This study presents a rapid screening method integrating a disposable three-electrode sensing chip, catechol-assisted cyclic voltammetry (CV), and a source-conditioned hybrid one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN). Experiments were performed using deionized water and two reclaimed-water matrices with ICP-MS-confirmed background boron concentrations of approximately 56 and 62 pg mL-1. Standard additions covered 0–500 pg mL-1, including the 100 pg mL-1 application threshold. Matrix-dependent electrochemical variation was addressed using source-specific background subtraction, local baseline correction, Z-score normalization, and first-derivative transformation. Boron-responsive potential regions were identified by sliding-window Pearson correlation with Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction. Region-of-interest features, processed CV waveforms, and water-source information were integrated by the hybrid 1D-CNN. Grouped partitioning is used to reduce leakage between training and evaluation subsets during model assessment. Preliminary measurements showed concentration-dependent changes in localized CV regions and substantial waveform differences among water matrices, demonstrating the limitations of transferring calibration directly from deionized water to reclaimed water. The proposed platform is intended as a rapid secondary verification tool rather than a replacement for online analyzers or ICP-MS. When an online analyzer reports an abnormal boron concentration, the electrochemical chip can provide an independent screening result before confirmatory laboratory analysis. This proof-of-concept demonstrates the potential of integrating disposable electrochemical sensing, matrix-aware signal processing, and compact deep learning for fit-for-purpose water-quality monitoring in high-technology reclaimed-water applications.

papers.abstract: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) provides a portable approach for measuring relative hemodynamic changes outside conventional neuroimaging environments, but wearable systems require transparent acquisition and processing pipelines before they can support reproducible physiological studies. This paper presents OpenHbO, a cross-platform acquisition and analysis platform developed around a biosignalsplux fNIRS sensor and wireless hub. The platform integrates hardware configuration, real-time optical signal visualization, event annotation, metadata-rich data export, offline reprocessing, and conversion of dual-wavelength optical measurements to relative oxygenated hemoglobin (HbO), deoxygenated hemoglobin (HbR), and total hemoglobin (HbT) changes using the Modified Beer-Lambert Law. The current implementation uses an age-dependent differential pathlength factor and a user-defined optical baseline. Technical feasibility was evaluated on a cohort of six healthy subjects using a single frontal measurement channel in two experimental paradigms: a 30-s breath-hold challenge and a 10-Hz graded electrical hand-pain stimulation protocol. The breath-hold group average showed a delayed, synchronized rise in both HbO and HbR (with HbO dominance) during apnea, followed by rapid post-apnea recovery and a distinct physiological undershoot. During electrical stimulation, both HbO and HbR concentrations increased concurrently with the rising stimulus intensity—reaching their maximum peaks at the pain threshold—and immediately plummeted below the baseline upon stimulus cessation. Because the current configuration does not include a short-separation channel, cerebral and superficial contributions to the recorded frontal signals cannot be separated. The observed changes should therefore be interpreted as event-associated frontal hemodynamic responses rather than isolated cortical activation. These preliminary findings support the technical feasibility of the OpenHbO acquisition and processing workflow and identify short-separation measurements as an important direction for future system development.

papers.abstract: The bend angle is the key quality characteristic of press-brake forming, yet production lines lack real-time, objective in-process angle measurement referred to an explicit angular reference. Existing optical solutions [1], [2] share two error sources—specular reflection from the metal surface and the camera mounting pose—which commercial systems suppress through closed proprietary hardware, a costly barrier for small job shops. This work presents the patterned-backlight junction-point differential method: a display behind the workpiece shows horizontal bright fringes serving as backlight and explicit angular reference; the workpiece appears as a dark silhouette, the junction points between fringes and silhouette are fitted to obtain the bending-leg orientation, and the same-frame fringe orientation is subtracted. Because reference and measurand are imaged in the same frame, a camera roll adds the same increment to both and cancels exactly in the difference—a property of the principle, not a correction. A precision design law, ≈ 2√3⟂/(√), links the localization noise ⟂, the geometric span , and the point count to the attainable precision—verified at 45∘ over eight fringe geometries. Under a controlled-laboratory optical-bench surrogate protocol (not an actual press brake) and for the two-dimensional projected angle of a single bending leg, the repeatability standard deviation is 0.0093–0.0376∘ over the full 15∘–120∘ range, with linearity 2 > 0.99 and residuals ≤ 0.028∘. papers.title: Passive Cholesteric Liquid-Crystal Thin-Film Sensor for Intraocular Pressure Warning
papers.authorsLine: Hsin-Yu Chou
papers.abstract: Continuous intraocular pressure monitoring may reveal pressure fluctuations that are missed by single measurements in the clinic. This study evaluated a battery-free optical sensing concept based on the pressure-responsive structural color of cholesteric liquid crystals (CLCs). Two device formats were investigated. Polydimethylsiloxane microchannels were fabricated using needle-based and single-wire molding, filled with CLC, and sealed to evaluate geometric control and short-term integrity. A planar CLC film was subsequently prepared by spin coating between polydimethylsiloxane substrates and tested at 25 ± 1 °C under an equivalent pressure of 20 mmHg. The single-wire process produced a channel width of 342 ± 2 μm. CLC filling reached 99%, and no visible leakage was observed over seven days. Under 20 mmHg, the characteristic optical wavelength shifted from approximately 495 to 563 nm, corresponding to a 68 nm displacement. The microchannel format enabled repeatable filling but produced a small optical area and comparatively large spectral variation associated with channel geometry, filling uniformity, interfaces, and observation angle. The planar film therefore provides a more suitable architecture for subsequent quantitative calibration. These preliminary results support CLC structural color as a low-complexity warning mechanism for smart contact-lens research, while pressure-response linearity, repeatability, temperature compensation, and curved-lens integration remain to be established.
